title: Laredo Project Would Keep Semi-Trucks Off Parts of Riverbank Drive
excerpt: The City of Laredo's Riverbank Realignment Project would realign Riverbank Drive and extend Mescalero Drive so semi-trucks use a new route to the World Trade Bridge instead of neighborhood streets in south Laredo.
content:
The City of Laredo is advancing a project that would keep semi-trucks off parts of Riverbank Drive, easing traffic in south Laredo and improving safety and traffic flow around the World Trade Bridge.

The Riverbank Realignment Project would realign Riverbank Drive and extend Mescalero Drive, creating a truck route to and from the World Trade Bridge. The project area covers Riverbank Drive, the Mescalero Drive extension, Loop 20 and Mines Road.

A project manager said the design phase is under way and a traffic study is in progress. The results of the study and public feedback will be brought back to the City Council at its next meeting.

No cost figure and no construction or completion date were stated for the project.

Update, Nov. 24: Some members of the Port of Entry Advisory Committee raised a concern about the plan, KGNS reported on Nov. 22: sending neighborhood cars to the same area where trucks leave the World Trade Bridge each day could create a new choke point. City engineering director Eliud De Los Santos described the plan to the committee. The project remains in the design phase, and the committee will revisit it at its next meeting.

Sources: City of Laredo, Nov. 22, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 22, 2026.
